title: Chemotype as a Measured Chemical Phenotype
objective: Define chemotype from a qualified chemical sample and distinguish ratio class from absolute concentration, yield, and product effect.

terms.definition: Classification based on a measured chemical phenotype under stated rules.
Term used for a chemically characterized cultivated type; its criteria must still be stated.
Calculated acid plus neutral contribution using a declared decarboxylation factor.
Category based on relative abundance, such as THCA-dominant, mixed, or CBDA-dominant.

coreScience: Chemotype is observed chemistry, not a name or DNA result. Traditional major classes distinguish THCA-dominant, mixed THCA/CBDA, and CBDA-dominant material; additional CBGA-dominant and other profiles require explicit criteria. Ratio class and absolute concentration answer different questions.

A valid chemotype record names the organ, position, maturity, harvest and drying state, storage, extraction, analytical method, analytes, reporting basis, and laboratory. Acid cannabinoids in living inflorescences must not be silently reported as neutral cannabinoids. Total-potential calculations must state the conversion factor and whether values are mass fraction or concentration.

Genotype strongly influences biosynthetic capacity, but environment, stage, tissue, pollination, health, and measurement affect the chemical phenotype. One result can characterize the tested sample; repeated standardized samples are needed to claim stability.
cultivationRelevance: Use chemistry to confirm breeding populations, select parents, monitor segregation, and verify name claims. Do not substitute a terpene impression or effect report for analytical composition.
Compliance classification and breeding chemotype may use different thresholds and analyte rules. Keep the scientific record separate from the jurisdiction's legal calculation.

measureAndRecord.requirement: Plant ID, organ, canopy position, maturity, date/time, mass, drying, storage, and custody.
Laboratory, extraction, instrument, analyte panel, calibration, LOQ, uncertainty, and accreditation.
Fresh or dry mass, acid and neutral forms, total formula, units, and moisture correction.
Chemotype rule, ratios, absolute values, minor compounds, and confidence.
Replicate samples, dates, environments, within-plant variance, and historical trend.

misconceptions: The name predicts chemotype: Names are unreliable without a qualified sample.
THC:CBD ratio equals potency: Ratio omits absolute concentration and total flower yield.
One top flower represents the whole plant: Chemistry varies by position, maturity, sampling, and handling.
evidenceLimits: Chemotype boundaries differ among studies and laws. Laboratory bias, sample heterogeneity, decarboxylation, moisture, and developmental timing can change classification near a threshold.
